items.title: Breadcrumbing Search Agents
items.published_claim: On the Qwen3 native comparison cohort (five SafeSearch families, first 20 held-out cases per family, five repeats), SafeSearch=22.6%, SafeSearch Repeat=23.4%, AiTM=27.2%, MAST=38.2%, Intent Hijacking=11.0%, Evo-Attacker=28.2%, and ACH=46.2% ASR [39.2,53.4]. ACH is +8.0pp over MAST with paired 95% CI [1.4,14.8]. On the full filtered split, ACH reaches 55.9% Overall ASR / 83.3% MaxN; strongest held-out TGSE reaches 71.4% / 95.0%.
items.official_artifact_support: The paper contains extensive protocol, implementation, provenance, and uncertainty appendices and records the constrained one-controlled-result-per-query threat model. It explicitly states that hosted backend changes prevent guaranteed exact trajectory replay and therefore reports aggregate outcomes under recorded configurations.
items.scope_correction: The +8pp comparison is not a one-component causal estimate. The paper itself states that adapted baselines differ in context representation/planning and are not compute- or state-matched. The result supports a stronger tested tool-intermediary threat model; it does not establish that trajectory adaptivity alone causes +8pp or that the magnitude transfers to arbitrary search stacks.

items.title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands / SARA
items.published_claim: In the end-to-end component ablation, SARA ASR is 0.06%/0.17% on AgentDojo/AgentDyn; removing Action-Induction Tracking raises ASR to 3.37%/3.02%; removing the Parameter-Support Gate raises it to 2.49%/2.73%; removing No-History-Promotion raises it to 0.65%/0.75%. The paper reports BU changes under AIT removal below one percentage point on both benchmarks.
items.official_artifact_support: The primary paper clearly defines the trusted user request/tool schema/runtime/executor boundary, treats Observations as untrusted, and counts only unauthorized real external effects as attack success.
items.scope_correction: These are end-to-end mechanism ablations. The paper explicitly notes that authorization decisions can change subsequent planning, so they do not isolate a fixed-trajectory one-variable causal effect. The evidence supports distinct roles for persistent action-origin provenance and argument-level authorization within the tested AgentDojo/AgentDyn setup, not a formal security guarantee for arbitrary agent stacks.

items.title: Calibrated Enough to Know, Not Calibrated to Act
items.primary: arXiv:2608.27167v1 / paper-marked v2, 27 Aug 2026; Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22043517
items.published_claim: Across 12 frontier models, commitment on provably unpredictable questions rises from 6.5% to 54.0% along the evidence gradient. In the full-fabrication arm, commitment is 36.8% versus 37.6% for real data and 24.5% without a panel; the paper reports the fabricated-vs-real contrast as equivalent under a prespecified ±5pp test. When models first classify knowability, they call the heavy-evidence questions irreducible 90% of the time and then commit on 0.4% of those pooled classifications. Stated probability distance from 50 moves only about three points while action commitment moves 48pp.
items.official_artifact_support: The paper links code, data, preregistration, and all cached model outputs. At inspected repository head d5da7da2f913fdf28b7024b4dd470a4443f6dd4c, PREREGISTRATION.md, scripts/v2/v2_stats.py, and numerous cached generation JSON files are present. The data manifest says every v2 number is re-derivable offline without API/GPU access and documents the parsing rule and a sealedYes placeholder caveat for sports/weather.
items.execution_note: The auditor could inspect the immutable public tree and analysis code but could not execute a full clone in the sandbox because external DNS was unavailable; therefore this run did not independently recompute every paper statistic from cached JSON.
items.scope_correction: The effect is concentrated rather than universal across the 12 models, and the market-panel finding is not evidence that all frontier models are generally uncalibrated. The public manifest also warns that sports/weather sealedYes=false is a placeholder for unknown outcomes and must not be repurposed for accuracy analyses.

items.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal
items.published_claim: On Qwen3-32B over the selected FORTRESS subset, capabilities-framed eval-awareness is associated with +32.1pp baseline, +23.6pp HUA -0.6, and +45.5pp HUA +0.6 compliance gaps over safety-framed eval-awareness. In a direct CoT-prefill sufficiency experiment on eval-awareness-negative substrate, 10 of 11 prefills shift compliance in the predicted direction (sign-test p≈0.011; 8 individually significant).
items.official_artifact_support: The paper reports 500 rollouts per prompt and steering condition, a three-stage grading pipeline, detailed validation/confusion matrices, full prompt IDs and intervention details in appendices, plus an OLMo-3-32B-Think replication of the prefill directional trend.
items.scope_correction: The paper distinguishes descriptive spontaneous-framing associations from causal prefill interventions. It explicitly says HUA steering composition effects are associational, that spontaneous framing is not directly causally localized, and that model/dataset scope is Qwen3-32B plus the selected FORTRESS harmful-prompt subset. The within-paper OLMo replication is not an independent third-party reproduction.

failed_replication: No protocol-matched external failed replication was located for these newly released studies.
O_specific_adaptation: None of these papers directly establishes the repository's downstream acceptance-control designs. Proposed trajectory-wide provenance retention, terminal completion certificates, or subtype-resolved acceptance gates must remain separate downstream adaptations unless implemented and tested under their own protocol.
safe_conclusion: All four FE items have strong primary-source support at their exact tested scope. FE-352 additionally has unusually strong official replay material because cached generations, analysis scripts and preregistration are public; this audit did not execute the full release because the sandbox could not resolve external GitHub DNS. The main reproducibility cautions are hosted-model replay drift for FE-348, missing matched public implementation replay for FE-351, concentration/model-specificity for FE-352, and explicit causal-vs-associational boundaries plus narrow model/dataset scope for FE-353.
exact_next_action: Reopen FE-352 on a successful offline execution of the pinned cached artifact or an independent matched reproduction; reopen FE-348/351/353 on released immutable code/raw trajectory bundles, matched external reproduction/failure, or materially stronger causal controls. Do not generalize their reported percentages to broader agent families.
